# v0.1.7: Drive9 study (sub-issue of #155)

Sub-issue of [#155](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/155).

One of three external studies feeding the v0.1.7 architecture refactor
migration, alongside the Cloudflare Computer study and the AgentFS study. They
complement the internal exploration study
([#156](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/156)): #156 maps what
LayerFS is; these three map the design space around it. Drive9 is the closest
analogue to LayerFS in the set, so this study should go the deepest.

Drive9 ([mem9-ai/drive9](https://github.com/mem9-ai/drive9), Go, Apache-2.0) is
a **server-side workspace kernel for AI agents**: a durable workspace that can
be mounted from any sandbox, forked for parallel attempts, checkpointed, rolled
back, and committed with server-side conflict detection. Its own framing —
"sandboxes are disposable, workspaces should not be"; local disks run the
process, Git stores the final result, Drive9 keeps the working state in between
— is the same problem LayerFS attacks, solved by a different architecture.

## Goal

A source-backed breakdown of Drive9:

- **Architecture:** the server/client split — what runs in the server, what runs
  in the sandbox, where authority lives, how the two communicate; and how a
  workspace, a mount, a fork, a checkpoint and a commit are represented.
- **Implementation details:** storage and journaling (`pkg/journal`,
  `pkg/datastore`, `pkg/backend`, the S3 Express append-log WAL), mount
  lifecycle (`pkg/mountcontrol`, `pkg/mountstate`, `pkg/mountsupervisor`), the
  object/filesystem layer (`pkg/objectfs`, `pkg/treebuilder`), server-side
  conflict detection on commit, tenancy and leadership (`pkg/tenant`,
  `pkg/leader`).
- **Interface:** the CLI (`cmd/drive9`), the server (`cmd/drive9-server`), FUSE
  mount semantics and POSIX compatibility
  (`docs/posix-compatibility-report.md`), and five client SDKs
  (`clients/drive9-{js,kotlin,py,rs,swift}`).
- **What LayerFS can learn — the point of the study:** where the two designs
  make different trade-offs (authority placement, fork/attempt representation,
  commit conflict handling, journaling, mount supervision), what each choice
  buys, and which of them should inform the v0.1.7 refactor or the 0.2.0 model
  — and which should not.

## Deliverable

One document under `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/drive9/` (folder initialized
with this work item), linked from the
[v0.1.7 checklist](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/main/docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/README.md)
when accepted. It records the exact snapshot commit it was written against.

## Sources

- Upstream: https://github.com/mem9-ai/drive9 (Go 1.25+, Apache-2.0)
- Local snapshot: `/Users/yifanxu/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/study/drive9` @ `cff6d29`
  (2026-09-05, "feat(fuse): add S3 Express append-log WAL support (#883)")
- In-tree docs: `docs/design-overview.md`, `docs/design/`, `docs/specs/`,
  `docs/plans/`, `docs/posix-compatibility-report.md`,
  `docs/openclaw-drive9-fuse.md`

## Boundary

- Source reads against the pinned local snapshot only: no builds, tests or
  benchmarks of the studied repo, no changes to it, and no LayerFS code changes
  from this issue.
- Every load-bearing claim carries a source reference (file, module or doc);
  behaviour that could not be verified is recorded as unknown.
- Performance claims are quoted only from Drive9's own material with
  citations; this study measures nothing.
- Observations that imply a LayerFS change are handed to the v0.1.7 checklist,
  not decided here.

## Starting map (snapshot, orientation only)

A descriptive snapshot to start from, not a frozen scope and not a substitute
for the study's own source reads.

```text
cmd/                # drive9 (CLI), drive9-server, drive9-migration, kubectl-drive9-migration
pkg/
  server/               # server-side kernel
  fuse/                 # sandbox-side FUSE path
  mount{control,path,state,supervisor}/   # mount lifecycle
  journal/              # journaling
  datastore/ backend/   # storage backends
  objectfs/ treebuilder/   # object + tree construction
  gitcache/ gitwsindex/   # Git integration
  leader/ tenant/ tenantctx/ meta/   # tenancy, leadership, metadata
  semantic/ embedding/  # semantic / auto-embedding features
  webdav/ s3client/ encrypt/ vault/  # other surfaces
clients/            # drive9-js, drive9-kotlin, drive9-py, drive9-rs, drive9-swift
internal/           # migration, schemaspec, e2ereport
docs/               # design-overview.md, design/, specs/, plans/, posix-compatibility-report.md
e2e/ blackbox/      # test harnesses
```

## Status

Study complete (2026-09-16). Deliverable:
`docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/drive9/architecture_overview.md` (pin:
`study/drive9` @ `cff6d29`). Completion report, research log, findings
summary, and unknowns are recorded in the issue comments. Observations are
handed to the #155 checklist as recommendations, not decisions.

comments.body:
**Study complete — deliverable written 2026-09-16.**

**Deliverable:** `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/drive9/architecture_overview.md` (930 lines: prose + citations + six architecture diagrams — Drive9's own presentation, deployment topology, layer model, commit/conflict flow, FUSE write staging, mount supervision).

**Pin:** upstream `https://github.com/mem9-ai/drive9` (Apache-2.0, Go 1.25+); pinned local snapshot `/Users/yifanxu/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/study/drive9` at `cff6d294b452b54a964de2217c137af303602be9` (2026-09-05, "feat(fuse): add S3 Express append-log WAL support (#883)").

**Research log:**

- Seven areas, one research subagent each, run in parallel: (1) server architecture & authority, (2) storage & journaling, (3) mount lifecycle & FUSE, (4) commit & conflict detection, (5) content representation & Git integration, (6) interfaces (CLI/API/SDKs), (7) tenancy, leadership & secondary surfaces. The suggested split from the issue was kept unchanged.
- Verification: ~20 citation spot-checks across all seven reports, plus first-hand reads of the load-bearing mechanisms — the layer commit handler (`pkg/server/fs_layer.go:873-977`), the preflight conflict algorithm (`:1623-1716`), `RollbackFSLayer`, both layered-filesystem design docs in full, the POSIX compatibility report, and the S3 Express append-log spec.
- Reconciliation: one cross-report contradiction found and resolved — rollback does **not** truncate layer entries (state flip + synthetic rollback event only; spec rule D17).
- Read-only everywhere: exactly one file written (the deliverable), nothing under `study/` modified, no builds/tests/benchmarks of either repo, no measurements taken.

**Strongest "what LayerFS can learn" findings** (full detail and verdicts in the deliverable):

1. **Adopt per-path revision claims** as 0.2 Proposal metadata — the prerequisite input for auto-reconciliation, which Drive9 itself never performs (detect-and-park only).
2. **Adopt write-time synchronous CAS** at Proposal admission — Drive9 rejects stale-claim upserts inside the insert transaction, "while the writer can still retry."
3. **Borrow-with-changes flatten-then-diff commit planning** (rules D18/D19) — diff the candidate's effective tree against live main and skip already-matching paths; the shape of reconciling an older Workspace against a newer Branch head.
4. **Avoid detect-and-park as the 0.2 conflict end-state** — no merge/resolve API, and a crash mid-commit strands the layer in `committing` with no public escape; keep LayerFS's single-transaction Commit + CAS.
5. **Adopt the client-staging lost-update fences** (PayloadBaseRev separated from CAS BaseRev, durable-watermark fencing, generation-token binding) as a review checklist for layerfs-fuse's spool.
6. **Borrow-with-changes mount supervision** (typed exit codes, local-only health — "backend outage ≠ FUSE death", transport-broken vs degraded classification, PID+creation-time identity) for layerfs-daemon's helper lifecycle.
7. **Server-side authority is mostly authorization engineering** — a live D1-A implementation (cloud-sqlite-vfs vocabulary); one-database-per-tenant matches "a Store per tenant is simple and probably right" for the hosted line.
8. **Record the append-log WAL as a design precedent** for the future `layerfs` VFS projection — hosting a `synchronous=FULL` SQLite database in a network-backed projection costs full-file reuploads per fsync; Drive9's mitigation (content-layout metadata, conditional tail append, 32-byte generation reset) is proven peer-system design.
9. **The tip-pin fork** (`origin_seq = MAX(entry_seq)`, never `durable_seq`) confirms LayerFS's pin-one-exact-head design at server scale; borrow the depth caps and transitive pin retention if Proposals ever chain.
10. **Borrow the POSIX suite menu** (pjdfstest/LTP/flock/pyxattr/fsx/fio/mdtest; Drive9 claims 8,941/8,941, vendor-reported) for 0.2 projection conformance — with LayerFS-side numbers independently measured, never inherited from a vendor report.

**Unknowns** (recorded in the deliverable): the server half of the append-log WAL lives in the external `tidbcloud/fs` repo; the production topology of the reference deployment is not determinable from the repo; no independent performance characterization exists (only Drive9's own quoted figures); `ReexecPreflight` has no production caller (fd-handoff is design-only); `tenantctx.TenantIDFromContext` has no non-test consumer; the go-fuse fork delta cannot be inspected from the snapshot; the POSIX report lacks environment details and an unsupported-behavior list; the design timeline rests on doc dates (single shallow commit); npm publication state is unverifiable offline; the L0/L1/L2 tiered-context and cross-tenant sharing features could not be fully traced to current status.

These observations are handed to the #155 checklist as recommendations, not decisions.

title: v0.1.7: Drive9 study — server-side agent workspace kernel: architecture, implementation, interface, and what LayerFS can learn
